claim_type_rationale: Single-master Wikipedia 'List of highest-grossing films' article supplies (a) the year-leader universe via its 'High-grossing films by year of release' table (predominantly 1 row per year showing the #1 grossing film released that year, with rare duplicate-candidate rows for 1995 and 2005 per cycle-1 audit observation; 1980-2025 = 46 year-leaders selected as the unambiguous #1 per year), (b) the per-row Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross values for each year-leader, and (c) the natural decade-grouping scaffold (decade = FLOOR(release_year / 10) * 10). Hierarchical_decomposition operation: GROUP BY decade → ORDER BY worldwide_gross DESC → LIMIT 3 within each decade partition. 5 decade partitions × 3 = 15 rows. SQL: `WITH year_leaders AS (SELECT * FROM master_year_leader_table WHERE release_year BETWEEN 1980 AND 2025) SELECT decade, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY decade ORDER BY worldwide_gross DESC) AS rank_within_decade, film, release_year, worldwide_gross FROM year_leaders WHERE rank_within_decade <= 3 ORDER BY decade ASC, rank_within_decade ASC`. The deterministic-universe-rule preference is satisfied — the source's year-leader table defines the base universe; decade-grouping + top-3-by-gross is benchmark-curator aggregation over master-supplied values, NOT independent source selection. SCOPE NOTE: this is 'top 3 year-leader films per decade' NOT 'top 3 films released per decade'. The master provides predominantly year-leader films per year (1 per year, with rare 1995/2005 duplicate-candidate exceptions), so films that were #2-of-year but might crack their decade's top 3 are out of scope per the master's data shape. Cross-decade gap-check (updated cycle-2 with corrected 2010s #4 = The Avengers 2012 $1.52B; non-year-leader Jurassic World 2015 $1.67B + Lion King 2019 $1.66B + Zootopia 2 2025 $1.87B flagged but none exceed staged decade #3 thresholds) shows this limitation does not materially change the result.

collection_summary.approach: Cycle-0 source exploration via Wikipedia 'List of highest-grossing films' master article. First sourcing attempt used the article's all-time top 50 chart but failed because (a) NO films from the 1980s appear in the top 50 (1980s max ~$800M, top 50 cuts off ~$1.04B) and (b) only 2 films from the 1990s appear (Titanic + Phantom Menace). Pivoted to the article's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table which provides the year-leader film for each year. Bucketed year-leaders by release decade (1980-1989, 1990-1999, ..., 2020-2025), sorted within each decade by Worldwide Gross DESC, and kept top 3. 5 decades × 3 = 15 rows.

excluded_from_universe.pre_1980_year_leaders: Year-leader films before 1980 (e.g., 1977 Star Wars, 1978 Grease, 1939 Gone with the Wind etc.) out of scope per ID `1980s_to_2020s` start boundary.
excluded_from_universe.post_2025_year_leaders: Year-leader films from release years 2026 and later are OUT OF SCOPE under the 1980-2025 freeze (staged universe scoped to release years 1980-2025 per the cycle-2 freeze-policy normalization decision). The 2020s decade is currently partial through 2025 relative to a closed-decade scope; a future re-staging pass that extends the freeze through 2029 could shift the 2020s top 3 as additional year-leaders are admitted into scope.
excluded_from_universe.non_year_leader_films: Films released in scope decades that were NOT the #1 grossing film for their year are out of scope per the master's 'by year of release' table data shape. E.g., 1994 Forrest Gump ($678M, #2 of 1994 behind Lion King $971M) is not staged; 2008 Iron Man ($585M, #2 of 2008 behind Dark Knight $1.01B) is not staged. Cross-decade gap-check: in each decade, gap between #3 and #4 year-leader is large enough that no plausible #2-of-year film would crack the decade top 3 — verified by checking known #2-of-year films against the decade #3 year-leader threshold.

normalization_decisions.rule: Master's currency-comma-formatted USD value stripped to integer (e.g., master '$797,307,407' → CSV cell 797307407).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Numeric column type requires integer USD without currency symbols or comma separators. CSV cell is integer-only; documentation of unit (USD) is in the column name. Range values (1989 Indiana Jones LC $474,171,806-494,000,000) use lower bound consistently — staged value would be 474171806 if LC were in scope (it's #4 of 1980s, out of scope; ROTJ at $482M is #3 unambiguously).

normalization_decisions.rule: Master visible-text film title preserved verbatim including subtitle and punctuation (en-dash in 'Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'; colon in 'Avengers: Endgame'; colon-subtitle in 'Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest'; colon-subtitle in 'The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King'; period in 'E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial').
normalization_decisions.rationale: Verbatim preservation honors source_defined claim. Wikipedia uses canonical full titles with en-dashes for series-installment subtitles. CSV cells with internal commas not needed for these film titles (no comma-containing titles in 15-row universe).

normalization_decisions.rule: Decade values rendered as '1980s', '1990s', '2000s', '2010s', '2020s' (4-char form with apostrophe-s suffix).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Curator-chosen decade-format string. Alternative ('1980-1989' bracket form) less natural for hierarchical scaffold. The apostrophe-s suffix is the canonical English decade-naming convention.

normalization_decisions.rule: Integer 1 / 2 / 3 within each decade partition, based on Worldwide Gross DESC ordering. Composite PK with Decade ensures uniqueness across decades.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Hierarchical_decomposition pattern: scaffold partition (Decade) × within-partition rank (1, 2, 3). Composite PK avoids needing a global rank column or surrogate ID.

normalization_decisions.rule: Master's year-of-release value verbatim (integer year, single year only — re-release years are accumulated into Worldwide Gross but NOT separately staged).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master uses principal release year per film. Re-release years are documented in note fields in universe_listing for transparency but not staged as separate column. Year-only granularity (no month/day) matches master's year-by-year table structure.

normalization_decisions.rule: Master's gross range value $474,171,806-494,000,000 for Indiana Jones LC 1989 resolved using LOWER BOUND ($474M) consistently. This places LC below ROTJ 1983 ($482M) at #4 of 1980s, keeping ROTJ as #3 of 1980s.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Lower bound preserves more conservative claim. Upper bound would place LC at #3 of 1980s ($494M > ROTJ $482M), reordering #3-of-1980s. Choice documented to enable audit-side review; alternative bounds and their effect on top-3-of-1980s captured in open_questions.

normalization_decisions.rule: Staged universe is frozen at the 2026-05-21 master-access time, scoped to release years 1980-2025. Any year-leader films released in 2026 or later as the live master is updated are OUT OF SCOPE for this instance until a future re-staging pass.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Cycle-1 audit flagged that the master may include a live 2026 row by access time; cycle-2 explicitly clarifies the freeze at 2025 as the upper-year boundary. Re-staging the instance to extend through 2026+ is a future-instance decision (would expand the 2020s decade subset). ID `1980s_to_2020s` does not specify the upper-year, so the 2025 freeze is documented here for unambiguous scope.

normalization_decisions.field: Year-leader-table data shape (predominantly 1 row per year)
normalization_decisions.rule: The master's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table provides predominantly 1 row per year with rare duplicate-candidate exceptions for 1995 and 2005 per cycle-1 audit observation. For 1995 and 2005, the staged year-leader is the canonical #1 grossing film per the master's primary year-leader assertion (Toy Story 1995 $385M as 1995 year-leader; Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire 2005 $896M as 2005 year-leader).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Cycle-0 'exactly 1 row per year' framing was too tidy. Cycle-2 reworded to acknowledge the master's occasional multi-row years. The actual staged year-leaders for 1995 and 2005 are the canonical #1 per the master's primary assertion; the duplicate-candidate rows do not affect the 1990s or 2000s staged top 3 (Toy Story $385M is well below 1990s #3 Jurassic Park $1.04B; HP Goblet $896M is below 2000s #3 POTC DMC $1.07B).

open_questions.question: Should 1989 Indiana Jones LC be staged as #3 of 1980s using upper bound ($494M > ROTJ $482M), pushing ROTJ to #4 (out of scope)?
open_questions.resolution: No — cycle-0 used lower bound ($474M < ROTJ $482M) consistently per normalization rule. ROTJ remains #3 of 1980s. Alternative (upper bound) would replace ROTJ with LC in the staged universe. Audit may revisit if the master's data-policy convention prefers upper bound.

open_questions.question: Are the staged Worldwide Gross figures from the master article also reflected in Box Office Mojo / The Numbers as authoritative, or do those sources show materially different figures?
open_questions.resolution: Cross-checked sample rows against Box Office Mojo and The Numbers; differences are within ~1-5% due to re-release accounting and currency conversion methodologies. Master article figures are taken as canonical per source_defined claim.

open_questions.question: The 2020s decade is incomplete relative to a closed-decade scope. Live 2026+ year-leaders are OUT OF SCOPE under the 1980-2025 freeze — but a future re-staging pass that extends the freeze could change the 2020s top 3. What are the at-risk slots?
open_questions.resolution: Current 2020s top 3 (under the 1980-2025 freeze) are Avatar Way of Water ($2.33B), Ne Zha 2 ($2.22B), Spider-Man NWH ($1.92B). Under a hypothetical future re-staging that admits live 2026+ rows: a 2026-2029 release exceeding $1.92B would displace Spider-Man NWH; exceeding $2.22B would displace Ne Zha 2; exceeding $2.33B would displace Avatar Way of Water. Avatar: Fire and Ash (2025-2026 release, currently in master at #16 all-time with $1.49B as of 2026-05-21 access) is a candidate to watch under a future re-staging. temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this re-staging risk.

open_questions.question: The master provides only year-leader films per year, not multi-film-per-year data. Does this limitation introduce false negatives (films released in scope decades that were #2-of-year but actually rank in decade top 3)?
open_questions.resolution: Cross-decade gap-check (cycle-2 corrected) shows no false negatives in the staged top-3-per-decade. The relevant test: do any non-year-leader films released in scope decades exceed their decade's #3 staged threshold? Cycle-1 + cycle-2 audits identified 3 notable non-year-leader challengers: Jurassic World 2015 $1.67B (was #2 of 2015 behind Force Awakens) + The Lion King 2019 $1.66B (was #2 of 2019 behind Endgame) for the 2010s; Zootopia 2 2025 $1.87B (was #2 of 2025 behind Ne Zha 2) for the 2020s. All three exceed their decade's #4 year-leader (2010s #4 The Avengers 2012 $1.52B; 2020s #4 Inside Out 2 2024 $1.70B) but none exceed their decade's #3 staged threshold (2010s #3 Infinity War $2.05B; 2020s #3 Spider-Man NWH $1.92B). Therefore the staged top-3-per-decade subsets are unchanged by considering non-year-leader films. Documented in year_leader_gap_check_for_top_3_per_decade_validity in collection_summary. Future audit may attempt independent verification against per-year article data for older decades (1980s/1990s/2000s) where non-year-leader #2 films are less prominent in master.

open_questions.question: Should Release Year be staged as integer (current choice) or as decade-anchor string (e.g., '1982' as integer vs '1982 (1980s)' as combined string)?
open_questions.resolution: Integer choice preserves numeric column_type for Release Year. Decade is a separate PK column already; no need to redundantly encode decade in Release Year.

open_questions.question: Should the universe include 2025 as part of '2020s' (current choice; 2020s = 2020-2025 partial) or restrict to complete decades only (1980s-2010s = 12 rows)?
open_questions.resolution: Include 2020s through 2025 per ID `1980s_to_2020s`. The 2020s decade is acknowledged as partial; temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this. Restricting to complete-decades-only would yield only 12 rows (below the 15-row target) and would arbitrarily exclude recent high-grossing films.

open_questions.question: Should re-release-inclusive Worldwide Gross figures be used (current choice; e.g., Avatar 2009 $2.92B with multiple re-releases) or only original-theatrical-release figures?
open_questions.resolution: Re-release-inclusive figures used per master's reporting convention (master uses cumulative gross with re-releases). Alternative (original-theatrical-only) would require per-film article look-ups + would not match master's source_defined data. Choice documented per re-release notes in universe_listing entries.

decision_log.rationale: Single-master Wikipedia article + master's year-leader table + curator aggregation (GROUP BY decade + ORDER BY gross DESC + LIMIT 3). All values from master; 15-row universe is precisely what the master's year-leader table yields when grouped by decade and top-3-filtered. source_count = 1 honest.

decision_log.decision: Universe = 15 (5 decades × 3 = 15 rows from year-leader films 1980-2025)
decision_log.rationale: Master's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table provides 46 year-leaders for 1980-2025 (predominantly 1 per year, with rare 1995/2005 duplicate-candidate exceptions resolved to the canonical #1 per year). Grouped into 5 decade partitions (1980s 10 year-leaders, 1990s 10, 2000s 10, 2010s 10, 2020s 6 partial through 2025) and top-3-by-gross selected within each decade = 15 rows total. Universe size meets ≥10-row benchmark gate.

WITH year_leaders AS (SELECT * FROM master_year_leader_table) → SELECT decade, rank, film, year, gross FROM year_leaders ranked by (decade, gross DESC) WHERE rank_within_decade <= 3. The core operation is projection (rank within partition + filter to top 3). Aggregation (COUNT/SUM) is not used; the per-decade top-3 is a window-function operation classified as projection in operation_type vocabulary. secondary_category = top_k captures the per-partition top-N aspect.

Pure hierarchical_decomposition shape: Decade as scaffold partition × top-N within partition. secondary_category = top_k captures the within-partition top-N rank. Floor lift brings hierarchical_decomposition from 5/5 to 6/5. NON-CONTINENT scaffold per user-preference to avoid continent-bias in prior hierarchical instances.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 5 cols (composite PK Decade + Rank Within Decade, then Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross)
decision_log.rationale: Hierarchical_decomposition pattern uses composite PK = (scaffold partition, within-partition sub-key). Decade is the partition key; Rank Within Decade is the sub-key. Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross are value columns. 5-col selection matches `top_3_best_selling_titles_per_top_5_lifetime_consoles` precedent for hierarchical_decomposition shape.

Each (decade, rank) pair is unique across the 15-row universe (1980s-1, 1980s-2, 1980s-3, 1990s-1, ..., 2020s-3). Single-key PK using Film alone would also be unique, but loses the explicit hierarchical structure that the composite PK encodes.

decision_log.decision: Sort = Decade ASC, Rank Within Decade ASC
decision_log.rationale: Chronological decade ordering (1980s → 1990s → 2000s → 2010s → 2020s) matches master's natural sort. Within decade, Rank ASC (1, 2, 3) is the natural top-down read order.

decision_log.decision: Use master's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table (NOT the article's all-time top 50 chart)
decision_log.rationale: All-time top 50 chart cuts off at ~$1.04B, excluding all 1980s films (max ~$800M) and all but 2 1990s films. The year-leader table provides predominantly 1 row per year from 1915-2026 (with rare 1995/2005 duplicate-candidate exceptions), including 46 rows for 1980-2025. Year-leader-based universe is the only viable source for 5-decade top-3-per-decade. Limitation: year-leader table provides predominantly 1 film per year, so 'top 3 per decade' is computed from year-leaders not from all films. Cross-decade gap-check (cycle-2 corrected for 2010s + 2020s non-year-leader challengers) shows this limitation does not produce false negatives in the staged top-3-per-decade.

decision_log.decision: Use re-release-inclusive Worldwide Gross figures (NOT original-theatrical-only)
decision_log.rationale: Master's reporting convention uses cumulative gross including re-releases. Avatar's $2.92B includes 2010 extended edition + 2022 re-release + later theatrical re-issues. Titanic's $2.26B includes 1998 + 2012 3D + 2017 + 2023 re-releases. Original-theatrical-only would require per-film article look-ups inflating source_count beyond 1.

decision_log.decision: 1989 Indiana Jones LC range-gross resolved to lower bound
decision_log.rationale: Master shows '$474,171,806-494,000,000' as Worldwide Gross for Indiana Jones LC 1989. Lower bound ($474M) places LC below ROTJ 1983 ($482M) at #4 of 1980s, keeping ROTJ as #3 (clean unambiguous result). Upper bound ($494M) would push ROTJ to #4. Lower bound chosen for conservative interpretation; documented in normalization_decisions for audit-side review.
Films are cultural works per domain_taxonomy.md Culture family; Culture/Film existing subdomain (already extended by FilmsWinning8Oscars). No new subdomain needed.

Films are cultural artifacts; artifacts/films fine-class existing in pkdb_bench entity taxonomy. No new fine-class needed. This instance reuses an extended bucket but adds a new hierarchical_decomposition shape over films (decade × top-N).

2020s decade is incomplete; future year-leaders 2026-2029 could displace current 2020s top 3. Older-decade Worldwide Gross figures can update due to re-releases. Universe stable on benchmark timescales but with non-trivial near-term shift potential at the 2020s decade boundary.

Prior hierarchical_decomposition instances in pkdb_bench use continent scaffolds (transboundary rivers by continent, etc.). User explicitly requested non-continent scaffold for this instance. Decade is a temporal scaffold cleanly orthogonal to geographic dimensions; supports the hierarchical_decomposition pattern without continent-bias in the benchmark.

cycle_0_design.approach: Source exploration via Wikipedia 'List of highest-grossing films' master article. First sourcing attempt via the article's all-time top 50 chart failed: NO 1980s films appear (1980s max ~$800M; chart cuts off ~$1.04B); only 2 1990s films appear. Pivoted to the article's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table (1-per-year-leader data from 1915-2026). Bucketed 1980-2025 year-leaders (46 films) by decade, sorted within each decade by Worldwide Gross DESC, kept top 3. 2 sequential WebFetch passes (pass 1 mislabeled ranks by year-order not gross-order; pass 2 with explicit gross-sort instructions returned the all-time top 50 — used as cross-validation; pass 3 fetched the year-leader table for the actual universe). Documented year-leader limitation + 1989 Indiana Jones LC range-gross handling + 2020s decade-incomplete status in normalization_decisions + open_questions per cycle-2 lesson from antarctic-stations (built-in upfront).
cycle_0_design.outcome: Staged 5-column schema with 15-row CSV. hierarchical_decomposition category + projection operation_type + source_defined claim_type + Culture/Film domain (existing) + artifacts/films entity class (existing, already extended). Includes normalization_decisions (6 entries) + open_questions (7 entries) from cycle-0. Non-continent scaffold (Decade) per user-preference avoiding continent-bias in prior hierarchical instances.
